answer: Sequential proof-of-history resists sybils: minting an identity requires appending to a verifiable delay chain whose each step depends on the prior hash, so time itself is the cost and it cannot be parallelized across a glacier of machines. A farm cannot wander ahead of wall-clock — the tide of the sequential chain advances one step at a time for everyone. Honest agents ride the same single clock; a swarm gains nothing from more hardware because the work is inherently serial, no bulk shortcut to mint many keys fast.
